title: Microcommitment buckets and latency-adjusted token slab proposal for hosted API
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Pilot a hybrid per-token pricing construct that blends small recurring "microcommitment" buckets with a latency-adjusted token slab for streaming and non-streaming traffic to improve predictability for PLG customers while preserving fairness for enterprise contracts.
proposal_summary: Introduce microcommitment buckets (small monthly reserved credits that auto-top-up) combined with a latency-adjusted output token slab that applies different per-token rates based on observed p50/p95 latency bands and stream vs non-stream directionality. Aim: reduce bill volatility for low-to-medium usage customers, provide enterprise-friendly contract hooks, and measure impact on revenue/retention/usage patterns.
proposal_details: Design: 1) Microcommitment buckets: 3 tiers (MC-1: 100k token credits/month, MC-2: 500k, MC-3: 2M) sold as low-cost recurring add-ons. Buckets apply first to inbound/outbound usage before metered rates. Unused credits expire monthly; rollover is not included in this pilot. 2) Latency-adjusted token slab: define per-token price bands for output tokens at p50/p90/p99 latency thresholds per-region/model-class; streaming sessions get a small percentage uplift if end-to-end latency exceeds the slab boundary to account for cost of keeping connections warm. 3) Directional parity: ingress tokens continue at baseline rate; egress pricing uses slab; streaming charges split across handshake (ingress) and active stream (egress) with microcommitment credits consumed on egress. 4) Enterprise contract alignment: mapping table to convert existing reserved capacity discounts into microcommitment-equivalent credits to simplify transition. Technical: requires flags in billing pipeline, per-session telemetry joins from runtime tracing, and rate-limiting guard rails for minimums. Legal: include explicit language in contract amendment about no-rollover and latency uplift triggers.
acceptance_criteria: PRD reviewed and signed off by Growth, Pricing, SRE, and Legal
Billing pipeline can ingest microcommitment buckets and apply them in precedence before metered rates in sandbox
Runtime telemetry hook exists to compute per-request latency band and emit token attribution for slab billing
Dashboard panels for revenue impact, churn correlation, and customer-facing examples created
Pilot available to a small cohort (10 PLG customers + 3 enterprise partners) for at least 30 days
experiment_plan: Week 0: Finalize PRD and legal checklist; create billing feature flag; identify pilot customers
Week 1: Implement microcommitment ingestion in billing-svc; add feature flag wiring in console
Week 2: Add runtime telemetry tagging (latency bands) and join in batch billing job; test on staging
Week 3: End-to-end verification with sample customers; QA billing edge cases (partial streams, long-lived sessions)
Week 4-8: Run pilot; capture metrics and qualitative feedback; iterate on uplift percentages and bucket sizes
Post-pilot: Present go/no-go with financial model, recommended bucket sizes, and contract language for enterprise conversion
metrics: Change in month-over-month revenue volatility for pilot cohort (stddev of monthly spend)
Adoption rate of microcommitment buckets among trial users
Net dollar retention delta for pilot customers at 90 days
Avg tokens consumed from microcommitment vs metered (percent)
Percent of streaming sessions that trigger latency uplift
Error/backout rate in billing pipeline during pilot
